title: footnote markers should be inline with the verses
summary: Footnote markers (the small ⓘ icons in Bible text) could end up alone at the start of a new line, cut off from the word they belong to. This PR glues each marker to the word just before it, so when a line wraps the word and its marker move together. It also moves a marker that came right after a poetry line break back onto the end of the line above, and slightly tightens the gap between the word and the marker.

links.label: Issue 1966: Footnote markers can be placed in awkward places

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use a desktop browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari). Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page looks like an older version, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac. You don't need to sign in for these tests.

setup.title: Make sure footnotes are turned on
setup.body: Open **Settings**, choose **Display & Theme**, and under **Scripture elements** make sure **Show footnotes** is turned on. Then go back to reading.

setup.title: Know how to make lines wrap differently
setup.body: Most tests ask you to change the width of the reading area so different words land at the end of a line. Drag the edge of the browser window to make it narrower and wider, slowly. On a phone, rotate between portrait and landscape instead. Keep an eye on the small ⓘ footnote markers as the text reflows.

sections.title: Footnote markers stay next to their word

tests.title: A footnote marker never starts a line on its own in regular prose
tests.why: This is the bug from the issue: the ⓘ marker sat alone at the start of a line, away from the word it explains.
steps: Open **Genesis 1** (any chapter with several ⓘ markers works).
Slowly drag the window narrower and wider, watching the ⓘ markers.
Stop whenever a marker lands near the right edge of a line, and look closely at it.
expected: Every ⓘ marker stays on the same line as the word just before it.
When there isn't room at the end of a line, the word and its marker move down to the next line together.
No line ever starts with an ⓘ marker.

tests.title: Markers stay attached in poetry
tests.why: Poetry (Psalms, Proverbs) is laid out line by line, and the PR moves a marker that came right after a line break back onto the end of the line above it.
steps: Open **Psalm 23**, then **Psalm 1**.
Find the ⓘ markers in the indented poetry lines.
Drag the window narrower and wider again.
expected: Each ⓘ marker sits at the end of (or inside) the poetry line whose word it follows, not alone at the start of the next line.
Poetry lines still break and indent the same way they did before; only the markers' positions change.

tests.title: Markers stay attached in red-letter text
tests.why: Words of Jesus are drawn differently from regular text, and the fix had to be applied there separately.
tests.before: If **Show red lettering** is off in **Settings** → **Display & Theme**, turn it on.
steps: Open **Matthew 5** (or another Gospel chapter with red words and ⓘ markers).
Find a marker inside or right after the red text.
Drag the window narrower and wider.
expected: Red-letter text still shows in red.
ⓘ markers next to red text stay on the same line as the word before them.

tests.title: Check the passage from the issue at phone width
tests.why: The screenshot in issue 1966 was a narrow, phone-sized layout. The exact passage isn't named, so this covers several chapters at that width.
steps: Make the window as narrow as it goes (about phone width), or open the preview on a phone.
Scroll through **Genesis 1**, **Psalm 23** and **John 1**, looking at every ⓘ marker.
expected: No line starts with an ⓘ marker.
No marker is cut off or pushed past the right edge of the screen, and the page doesn't scroll sideways.

tests.title: The gap between a word and its marker looks right
tests.why: The PR changed how the space before the marker is made. It should look about the same as before: a small gap, not a wide one and not touching.
steps: Open **Genesis 1** and look closely at a few ⓘ markers in the middle of a line.
expected: There's a small, even gap between the word and its ⓘ marker, similar to a normal space.
The marker is not jammed against the word, and there isn't a large gap or a double space before it.
The text after the marker still has a normal space before the next word.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Clicking a marker still opens its footnote
steps: In **Genesis 1**, click an ⓘ marker.
Read the window that opens, then close it with the **X** button.
expected: A footnote window opens with that footnote's text.
Clicking the marker does not select the verse.
The window closes normally.

tests.title: Turning footnotes off still hides the markers
steps: Open **Settings** → **Display & Theme**, and turn off **Show footnotes**.
Go back to **Genesis 1** and **Psalm 23**.
Turn **Show footnotes** back on afterwards.
expected: No ⓘ markers are shown.
Words that used to sit next to a marker still have a normal space before the next word (no words run together).
In Psalm 23, the poetry lines still break where they should.

tests.title: Highlighting a verse with a footnote still works
tests.why: The fix trims the space at the end of text right before a marker, and highlights are placed by position in the text.
tests.before: Sign in if highlighting asks you to.
steps: In **Genesis 1**, tap or click a verse that has an ⓘ marker to select it.
Add a highlight in any color.
Look at the highlighted verse, then remove the highlight.
expected: The whole verse is highlighted, including the words just before the marker; no word is left out or shifted.
The marker is still in the same place and still clickable.
Removing the highlight works normally.

notCovered: The new automated test checks the spacing around the marker in a simulated browser that can't measure real line wrapping, so the wrapping itself is only checked by the tests above.
The exact chapter from the issue screenshot isn't named in the issue. If you know which passage it was, check it too and mention it in your results.
